findings.evidence: MeasureTheory/Measure/ProbabilityMeasure/Convex.lean:29-34: declarations are in the root namespace "rather than under `TauCeti`, since the type is Mathlib's; that is what lets `P.convexComb hab Q` be written as dot notation". CategoryTheory/Action/Transitive.lean:24-27 and RepresentationTheory/Induction/Transitivity.lean:109-111 say `scripts/lint-dot-notation.py` rejects a Mathlib type namespace nested inside `TauCeti` "because dot notation on that type then fails to elaborate". Mathlib declares `structure CommHopfAlgCat` (mathlib/Mathlib/Algebra/Category/CommHopfAlgCat.lean:27). No file in the repo uses such dot notation: every call site spells the prefix, e.g. `Subgroup.normalizerQuotient torus` (RepresentationTheory/SU2/Weyl/Basic.lean:212) for the baselined `TauCeti.Subgroup.normalizerQuotient`.
findings.fix: Delete the paragraph (same paragraph at Center/IdentityComponent.lean:29-30 for `H.reducedCenterIdentityComponentDefiningIdeal`), or, if the elaboration really works, back it with an actual in-repo use and reconcile it with the lint's stated rationale.
findings.issue: New paragraph "Open `TauCeti` to use this API with dot notation, such as `H.reducedCenterCoordinateMap`, alongside `H.reducedCenterDefiningIdeal` and `H.quotientReducedCenterIso`" documents a usage pattern that does not work: these declarations live in `TauCeti.CommHopfAlgCat`, not the root `CommHopfAlgCat` namespace of the receiver's type.

findings.evidence: Center/Reduced.lean:80-81 documents the analogous `centerDefiningIdeal_le_reducedCenterDefiningIdeal` with both readings: "The center ideal is contained in the reduced-center ideal. Contravariantly, the reduced center is a closed subgroup of the center."
findings.fix: State both readings as the sibling lemma does, e.g. "The reduced-center ideal is contained in the identity-component ideal. Contravariantly, the identity component is a closed subgroup of the reduced center."
findings.issue: Docstring "The identity component of the reduced center is contained in the reduced center" gives only the geometric reading of `reducedCenterDefiningIdeal H ≤ reducedCenterIdentityComponentDefiningIdeal H`, whose literal ideal inclusion runs the other way; read as a statement about the ideals it is backwards.

summary: Both files gained a new docstring paragraph advertising dot notation (`H.reducedCenterCoordinateMap`) that the repo's own documented rule and dot-notation lint say does not elaborate for declarations nested under `TauCeti`. One new lemma docstring also states only the geometric reading, in the direction opposite to the literal ideal inclusion.
